subject: Prod-like POC: access & network handshake
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@mediq.com>, procurement@mediq.com
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prod-like POC: access & network handshake

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, we want to stand up a production-like POC environment so Mediq can validate latency and cost for the clinical transcription flow. To make the MAP actionable, below are the minimal access items we need from your side and proposed dates: 

- Org setup & SSO invite (team-admin role): requested by 2027-03-18
- API key issuance + token scope (read/write): requested by 2027-03-18
- IP allowlist for Redwood token endpoints: add our egress IPs by 2027-03-22
- VPC peering request (Mediq -> Redwood): peering window 2027-03-24 to 2027-03-25

I attached a simple network diagram and a short spreadsheet with required fields for org creation. Can procurement pull the DocuSign for the POC T&Cs? If you prefer, we can split the work: we can create the org invite and you approve, or your admin can send.

Next steps: if the dates above look ok, I’ll send a one-page MAP with responsibilities and gap owners. If any of these dates are unrealistic, tell us which items need more lead time.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: mediq-network-diagram.pdf, redwood-poc-reqs.xlsx

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice —
> 
> Thanks again for taking the call this morning...

Hi Sofia —

This looks reasonable. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) For the API keys: can you confirm the token validation endpoint and whether keys need CIDR-scoped restrictions?
2) For IP allowlist: our security team will only open onshore egress ranges; please provide the exact egress IPs you want us to allow.
3) VPC peering: we typically need a brief peering worksheet + route table change window. Our infra lead requests a 2-hour maintenance window; can Redwood commit an engineer for the cutover?

Procurement — I’ve looped you for DocuSign and the POC SOW.

Alice Park
Head of Integrations, Mediq
alice.park@mediq.com | x412
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, infra-oncall@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod-like POC: access & network handshake

Thanks Alice — quick responses inline and next-step assignments:

1) Token endpoints: https://auth.redwood.com/token and https://api.redwood.com/v1. Keys can be CIDR-scoped; we recommend scoping both at the org-level and token-level.

2) Egress IPs: our current onshore egress pool (for the US region) is: 34.82.210.100/32, 34.82.210.101/32, 34.82.210.102/32. If you prefer a broader range, tell us and we’ll provide a /29.

3) VPC peering: we can commit a Redwood infra engineer (Marcus) to the 2-hour window. Proposed peering slot: 2027-03-24 02:00–04:00 PT (8:00–10:00 UK). Marcus will run the peering steps and validate routes.

I’ve added a one-page MAP in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MediQ-POC with responsibilities (owner column). Sofia — if you can send the MAP and the DocuSign request to procurement, we’ll mark org invite and keys as done once your admin confirms the email address.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
